record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: For every Boolean function f on n input bits, can one design a catalytic branching program with 2^{O(n)} possible start nodes and total size 2^{O(n)} · O(n) that computes f while restoring the initial catalytic state?

evidence.quote: Girard et al. [GKM15] define catalytic branching programs in the following way: rather than having a single start node ... we have m different start nodes ... The catalytic property ... states that on input x, each start node τ must reach exactly the end node labeled with f (x) and τ.
Problem 17. Design a catalytic branching program with 2O(n) start nodes and total size 2O(n) · O(n) for any function f .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A catalytic branching program on $n$ Boolean input variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ is a finite directed acyclic multigraph in which:
- each non-sink node is labeled by an input variable $x_i$ and has exactly two outgoing edges, labeled $0$ and $1$;
- there is a distinguished set $S$ of start nodes;
- each sink (end node) carries a label of the form $(b,\tau)$ with $b\in\{0,1\}$ and $\tau\in S$.

On input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, starting from a node $v$ the program follows, at each non-sink node labeled $x_i$, the outgoing edge labeled $x_i$ until a sink is reached; denote this sink by $\mathrm{end}(v,x)$.

The program is said to compute a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ catalytically if for every start node $\tau\in S$ and every input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$,
$$\mathrm{end}(\tau,x) = (f(x),\tau).$$
The size of the program is its total number of nodes.

Question: Does every Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ admit a catalytic branching program computing it with $|S|=2^{O(n)}$ start nodes and total size $2^{O(n)}\cdot O(n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Known constructions (Potechin 2017 and follow-ups by Cook–Mertz and Robere–Zuiddam) achieve amortized linear size only with doubly exponential numbers of start nodes, or higher per-program size with fewer start nodes. No construction is known matching simultaneously $2^{O(n)}$ start nodes and total size $2^{O(n)}\cdot O(n)$ for arbitrary Boolean functions, and the question is listed as an open problem in the recent literature on catalytic branching programs.

status_evidence.title: Trading Time and Space in Catalytic Branching Programs
status_evidence.snippet: Tradeoffs between number of start nodes and per-program size for catalytic branching programs; matching simultaneously 2^O(n) start nodes and near-linear amortized size for arbitrary f remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Existing tradeoffs do not yield 2^{O(n)} start nodes together with total size 2^{O(n)} · O(n) for general Boolean functions.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic Branching Programs from Groups and General Protocols
status_evidence.snippet: Robere–Zuiddam construct catalytic branching programs from group-based protocols; the regime of singly exponential start nodes with near-linear amortized size for all f is not achieved.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art constructions still fall short of the desired simultaneous bounds.
